# LaunchDarkly

> LaunchDarkly is a runtime control platform for software and AI agents. Its two products, CodeControl and AgentControl, let teams release code behind feature flags, roll out changes progressively, run experiments, observe releases, and adjust AI agent behavior in production without redeploying.

LaunchDarkly was founded in 2014 in Oakland, California. CodeControl covers feature flags, targeting, progressive rollouts, and guarded releases for application code, including AI-generated code. AgentControl covers configuring, evaluating, and guarding AI agents, prompts, and models in production.

Product documentation, SDK references, and tutorials have their own index at https://launchdarkly.com/docs/llms.txt. Any documentation page is available as Markdown by appending `.md` to its URL. The REST API reference is at https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api.

## Company overview

- [About LaunchDarkly](https://launchdarkly.com/about-us/): Company background, including its 2014 founding in Oakland, California, by Edith Harbaugh and John Kodumal, and its expansion from feature management to runtime control for code and AI agents.
- [Contact us](https://launchdarkly.com/contact-us/): General contact form for questions about LaunchDarkly products and services.
- [Contact sales](https://launchdarkly.com/contact-sales/): Form for talking to the LaunchDarkly sales team about plans, pricing, and product fit.
- [Request a demo](https://launchdarkly.com/request-a-demo/): Form for scheduling a live demo of the LaunchDarkly platform.
- [Careers](https://launchdarkly.com/careers/): Information about working at LaunchDarkly; open positions are listed on Greenhouse.
- [Press and analysts](https://launchdarkly.com/press-and-analysts/): Press resources, including downloadable brand assets, office addresses in Oakland, California, and London, UK, and social channels.
- [Compare LaunchDarkly](https://launchdarkly.com/compare/): Index of comparison pages against Optimizely, Statsig, Unleash, Harness, Datadog, and Firebase Remote Config, plus a build-vs-buy comparison with homegrown feature flag systems.
- [Partner program](https://launchdarkly.com/partner-program/): Program for technology partners, covering the Integration Framework for building integrations into LaunchDarkly, partnership support, and visibility to LaunchDarkly customers in the app.
- [Security](https://launchdarkly.com/security/): LaunchDarkly's security and privacy program, including SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, FedRAMP authorization, and Data Privacy Framework certification, plus data-security features such as private attributes.
- [Changelog](https://launchdarkly.com/changelog/): Feed of new LaunchDarkly product features and improvements.
- [Subscription terms](https://launchdarkly.com/policies/subscription-terms/): Terms of Service for Developer tier and Foundation self-service customers, effective September 8, 2025.
- [Terms of Service for Starter and Pro customers](https://launchdarkly.com/terms-of-service/): Terms of Service that apply to customers on Starter and Pro plans.

## Products

- [AgentControl](https://launchdarkly.com/platform/agent-control/): Product page for AgentControl, which governs AI agents in production with real-time guardrails, online evaluations, automatic correction when thresholds are breached, and instant rollback.
- [CodeControl](https://launchdarkly.com/platform/code-control/): Product page for CodeControl, which controls code releases, including AI-generated code, with feature flags, targeting, progressive rollouts, guarded releases with performance thresholds, and kill switches.

## How LaunchDarkly works

- [Platform overview](https://launchdarkly.com/how-it-works/platform/): How the LaunchDarkly platform works as a runtime control layer for code and agent behavior in production.
- [Platform architecture](https://launchdarkly.com/how-it-works/platform-architecture/): How SDKs embedded in the application runtime and a streaming architecture based on server-sent events (SSE) release or roll back a change within 200ms worldwide, and how the platform handles security and resilience.
- [Feature flags](https://launchdarkly.com/how-it-works/feature-flags/): How LaunchDarkly feature flags handle targeting, progressive releases, and automatic recovery in production.
- [Observability](https://launchdarkly.com/how-it-works/observability/): How LaunchDarkly connects errors, regressions, and AI agent behavior drift to the release, flag, or version that caused them, and remediates automatically when guardrails are breached.
- [Experimentation](https://launchdarkly.com/how-it-works/experimentation/): How teams design and run experiments on features, models, and prompts, including audience targeting, assignment logic, and mutual exclusion, in the same tool they use to ship.
- [Agent integrations](https://launchdarkly.com/how-it-works/agent-integrations/): How to use LaunchDarkly from Claude Code, Cursor, the terminal, or an IDE through its MCP server and agent skills, such as `npx skills add launchdarkly/agent-skills --skill onboarding -y`.

## Solutions

- [Control AI agents](https://launchdarkly.com/solutions/control-ai-agents/): Governing, monitoring, and correcting AI agents in production with AgentControl, without redeploying.
- [Release AI-built code](https://launchdarkly.com/solutions/release-ai-built-code/): Releasing AI-generated code with predefined guardrails and automated rollouts using CodeControl.
- [Optimize AI performance](https://launchdarkly.com/solutions/optimize-ai-performance/): Comparing models and measuring AI agent cost and performance in real time with AgentControl.
- [Run experiments](https://launchdarkly.com/solutions/run-experiments/): Running AI and product experiments in production and measuring results without redeploying.
- [Self-heal systems](https://launchdarkly.com/solutions/self-heal-systems/): Detecting production issues in code and AI agents and remediating them automatically, without a redeploy.
- [LaunchDarkly and AWS](https://launchdarkly.com/solutions/launchdarkly-aws/): Using LaunchDarkly on AWS to decouple deployment from release, migrate to the cloud, and ship AI agents and code.
- [Enterprise prompt management](https://launchdarkly.com/solutions/enterprise-prompt-management-tools/): Versioning, governing, and A/B testing LLM prompts across OpenAI, Anthropic, and Amazon Bedrock without shipping code.
- [AI observability](https://launchdarkly.com/solutions/ai-observability-platform/): Monitoring AI agents and models in production and fixing issues without redeploying.

## Personas

- [AI engineers](https://launchdarkly.com/persona/ai-engineers/): How AI engineers configure, benchmark, release, observe, and improve AI agents in production, including catching agent drift.
- [Development teams](https://launchdarkly.com/persona/development-teams/): How software development teams use feature management, runtime control, and automatic remediation.
- [DevOps and SRE teams](https://launchdarkly.com/persona/devops-site-reliability-engineer-teams/): How DevOps and site reliability engineering teams manage releases, reduce production risk, and automate rollback.
- [Product managers](https://launchdarkly.com/persona/product-managers/): How product managers release features, experiment in production, and measure impact.
- [Data scientists](https://launchdarkly.com/persona/data-scientists/): Statistical methods, metric governance, and scale for teams that run experimentation programs.

## Pricing

- [Pricing](https://launchdarkly.com/pricing/): Plan tiers and prices: Developer ($0 per month with unlimited seats), Foundation (pay as you go at $10 per service connection and $8.33 per 1,000 client-side MAU per month), and Enterprise (custom pricing), plus the Guardian release-safety add-on.
